FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A01
Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped and yellow or green, whereas a triangle sign with cut-off points is displayed on slow-moving vehicles such as farm vehicles [A01].
Why it matters: group sign shapes; difficulty medium; prereq sec06-F04; confusables sec06-F04, sec06-F03
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: FXP0033
A regulatory sign is a white rectangle that states a rule, whereas a warning sign is usually a yellow or green diamond that flags a danger, and the shape alone tells them apart when the face is obscured [FXP0033] [A01] [A02].
Why it matters: group sign shapes; difficulty medium; prereq sec06-F06; confusables sec06-F06, sec06-F04
Source: [FXP0033 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A02
Passing is judged by the line nearest your lane: a broken line on your side allows a pass when clear, while a solid line on your side forbids it even if the far side is broken [A02].
Why it matters: group passing lines; difficulty high; prereq sec06-F08; confusables sec06-F09, sec06-F08
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A02
Double solid yellow lines separate opposing directions on an undivided multilane highway, while broken white lines separate lanes moving the same way [A02].
Why it matters: group line colors; difficulty medium; prereq sec06-F07; confusables sec06-F08, sec06-F27
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A03
A lane change after completing a turn is normal driving, while a lane change during the turn is an illegal maneuver [A03].
Why it matters: group lane use; difficulty low; prereq sec06-F13; confusables sec06-F14, sec06-F13
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A04
Work zone signs are orange and diamond- or rectangular-shaped to warn of hazards ahead, and a flagger has legal authority to control traffic and must be obeyed [A04].
Why it matters: group work zones; difficulty medium; prereq sec06-F23; confusables sec06-F23, sec06-F24
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0037]
